lessons.title: The robot prints
lessons.practice_summary: reading what print shows, one line at a time

introductions.explanation: print writes its given text or number. Source quote marks are not printed; capital and small letters stay as written.
Read top to bottom: each print adds a line without clearing earlier lines. In choices, then means the next screen line, not printed text.
introductions.example: GO then 2 means GO on one line and 2 on the next.

introductions.explanation: A value on its own is valid code but does not write a screen line. Print adds lines in order without clearing earlier ones; then means the next line in choices.
introductions.example: Bare 8 and bare "WAIT" stay quiet; print("WAIT") shows WAIT.

lessons.title: Pockets
lessons.practice_summary: following the numbers held by named pockets

introductions.explanation: Assignment stores a number quietly. An unquoted name tells print which number to read; quoted text writes its word.
introductions.example: pocket = 1 stores 1; print(pocket) reads 1; print("pocket") writes pocket.

introductions.term: The latest number for each name
introductions.explanation: A new assignment replaces only that name's number, not earlier screen lines.
introductions.example: After pocket = 2 and spare = 9, print(pocket) still shows 2.

introductions.explanation: blue = red reads red's number now. Later changing red leaves blue alone; either name can still receive a new number.
introductions.example: If red holds 4, blue = red gives blue 4; red = 9 later leaves blue at 4.
